answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a correlated-behavior fee multiplier: the network measures how tightly each identity trades with the same small circle, like timber stacked on one narrow ledge. Identities whose counterparties mirror each other pay fees that rise steeply with clustering, while diverse traders pay almost nothing. A sybil farmer's thousand fakes trade in a closed loop, so every fake pays the top fee on every move; one honest agent with varied counterparties trades cheaply. Cloning keys multiplies the fee bill, not the profit.
